- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

**Root cause analysis** (verified on opencode 1.18.25, Windows 10 19041, Windows Terminal, admin pwsh 7.6.5):

**Why the title gets destroyed:** on win32 the copy path spawns an external `powershell.exe` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) child process to run `Set-Clipboard` — `packages/tui/src/clipboard.ts:86-92`:

```ts
if (os === "win32" && has("powershell.exe")) {
  await command(
    "powershell.exe",
    ["-NonInteractive", "-NoProfile", "-command",
      "[Console]::InputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Set-Clipboard -Value ([Console]::In.ReadToEnd())"],
  )
}
```

That child process shares the parent's console, and PowerShell 5.1 resets the console title to `Windows PowerShell` on startup. The tab title momentarily becomes `Windows PowerShell`, then falls back to the parent admin shell's default `Administrator: Windows PowerShell` — matching the two-step flicker other users report.

**Why it never comes back:** the terminal title is only set by a `createEffect` that runs when `route`/`session` changes — `packages/tui/src/app.tsx:452-471`:

```ts
renderer.setTerminalTitle(`OC | ${title}`)
```

A copy operation never re-runs that effect, so the title is not re-asserted after being clobbered.

**Possible fixes:**
1. Avoid the external PowerShell round-trip (write directly via Win32 clipboard, or use OSC 52) — this would also remove the ~1s overhead noted in #39722
2. Cheap fix: re-assert the title after the copy promise resolves

**Workaround for anyone affected:** run the `terminal.title.toggle` command twice (off → on) — this re-triggers the effect and restores the title immediately. Switching sessions away and back also works.

For anyone landing here from the issue: ways to keep this clean today, before and after this PR.

**On released versions (no PR needed):**

1. Git-wise you are already safe: opencode writes a `.gitignore` inside `.opencode` covering node_modules and the generated manifest files, so nothing reaches your commits. The clutter is filesystem-only.
2. Shared `.opencode` symlink: make `<project>/.opencode` a symlink to one shared directory (e.g. `~/.local/share/opencode/workspace`). The dependency install happens once, plan files land in a single place, and per-project agents/commands keep working. One caveat: an `opencode.json` inside the shared directory would apply to every project linked to it. Add `.opencode` to `~/.config/git/ignore` so no repo ever tracks the symlink.
3. `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1` stops the per-project dependency installs, but also disables per-project `AGENTS.md` and config discovery. Only viable if you keep everything global.
4. Periodic cleanup of `.opencode` works, but opencode reinstalls on the next open, so it is a treadmill.

**With this PR:**

Options 1-4 become unnecessary. Set `plans_directory` (e.g. `~/.local/share/opencode/plans`) and/or `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PLUGIN_DEPS=1` in your environment, and project directories stay completely untouched.

### Environment

- OpenCode 1.18.20
- macOS, Darwin 25.5.0
- Homebrew installation

### Reproduction

A reviewer subagent launched two parallel `webfetch` calls with `timeout: 60`.

### Result

Both calls were still `running` with no end timestamp 55 minutes later. Two sibling reviewers completed, but the affected child and its parent remained `busy`.

The OpenCode server and SQLite stayed responsive.

### Expected

The fetches should fail after 60 seconds and allow the child and parent sessions to unwind.

---

### Environment

- OpenCode 1.18.20
- macOS, Darwin 25.5.0
- Homebrew installation

### Reproduction

Starting OpenCode from `$HOME` caused three Explore agents to launch four `rg --hidden ... .` searches.

### Result

The searches entered CloudStorage, backups, and unrelated files. They were still running 42–45 minutes later, leaving the child and parent sessions `busy`.

The processes were mostly waiting on cloud filesystem I/O, so the failure appeared as a low-CPU freeze.

### Expected

Explore should search only the detected project or worktree unless broader access is explicitly requested.

This appears related to #41379.

We hit the same failure on OpenCode 1.18.20: two `webfetch` calls with `timeout: 60` remained running for 55 minutes and kept the reviewer and parent session busy. Details are in our comment on #45229.

A few questions:

- Would a regression test fit here where headers arrive but the body never finishes? The existing `withFetch` fixture may support it.
- Is the `Effect.fail` change intended to alter v1 behavior? The surrounding `Effect.orDie` calls appear to convert it back to a defect.
- Does the parameter snapshot need updating for the new bounds and description?
- Would you prefer keeping this PR focused on the body timeout and handling the validation/error changes separately?

Fresh reproducible occurrence on 2026-08-30 UTC, affecting both Go and Zen inference while credential-authenticated catalogs remain available.

Direct minimal probe results at 2026-08-30 01:06:46 UTC:

- `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/models` -> HTTP 200
- `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` with `deepseek-v4-flash` -> HTTP 401
- `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` -> HTTP 200
- `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/messages` with `claude-sonnet-5` -> HTTP 401

The inference probes were deliberately small: one plain text turn per provider, no tools, no streaming, no retries, and no capability/load test. A catalog request was made only after the inference 401 to distinguish invalid credentials from an inference-only block. Balances/subscriptions are active. Reissuing credentials did not resolve the condition.

This strongly suggests an account/workspace or upstream inference-policy block rather than an invalid key, model typo, endpoint mismatch, or insufficient balance. The same integration had previously completed live turns with nonzero usage before transitioning to this state.

Could a maintainer please clarify:

1. Which policy or automated risk/compliance condition causes authenticated catalogs to remain HTTP 200 while all paid inference is HTTP 401?
2. Is direct use of the documented Go/Zen endpoints from a custom coding-agent gateway permitted, including small tool, cancellation, and resume compatibility checks?
3. What is the private support/appeal channel where I can provide the account email, workspace ID, request IDs, and API-key identifiers without posting credentials publicly?
4. Could the API return a bounded machine-readable reason (for example `account_suspended`, `workspace_blocked`, or `upstream_policy_blocked`) instead of a generic 401 so clients do not misdiagnose this as an invalid key?

I will not post API keys or full account identifiers in this public issue, but can provide them privately to the team.

Requesting that the existing \ppearance.fontSize\ setting actually be applied to the UI.

Currently the value is persisted but has no visible effect:

- The settings init effect only applies font families (\--font-family-mono\, \--font-family-sans\) to CSS variables; no font-size variable is ever set — \packages/app/src/context/settings.tsx\
- The embedded terminal is initialized with a hardcoded \ ontSize: 14\ — \packages/app/src/components/terminal.tsx\

As a result the only way to scale text is page zoom (Ctrl +/-), which enlarges the entire UI including chrome/titlebars.

Additionally, it would be great if a conversation-only font size option were considered, so chat text can be enlarged independently of the rest of the UI.

Happy to help test once a fix lands.
